extraction.program_note: the program is committed in this directory as extract.awk and is the program that was actually run; run it as: printf 'kind\tlog_line\tengine_started_local\tpayload\n' > engine-metrics.tsv, then awk -v lo=12627 -v hi=13420 -v R="$INSTALL_ROOT" -f extract.awk "$ENGINE_LOG" >> engine-metrics.tsv. The install root is passed in at run time, so neither this manifest nor the program contains an absolute personal path. Syntax note: every condition is on one line because the default awk on this host is mawk, which rejects a condition continued across lines. Re-running extract.awk reproduced this TSV byte for byte at 15 693, at 17 233, at 18 689, at 19 664 and at 20 648 log lines
extraction.program: see extract.awk in this directory. Its whitelist is: engine_start lines; 'strata generate: expert cache N slots'; 'strata serve: prompt chunk auto'; 'strata mtp: draft layer loaded'; 'strata generate: mtp:' (MTP refusal / allocation failure); 'strata serve: prompt N tokens = …'; and the 'KV streaming', 'decode expert cache hit rate' and 'conversation cache' request counters. Usage text, ggml_cuda_init lines, load_hparams warnings and route-tail-skip counters are not selected

limitations: prompt identity across sessions is inferred from identical prompt token counts (12719 tokens in six sessions — five without MTP and one with MTP; 53 tokens as a warm-up probe in every session); the prompt text itself is private and unpublished

the cold-prefill figures quoted in docs/findings.md section 1 all come from requests with 0 reused KV tokens, i.e. cold-cache full prefills after an engine restart. This dataset also contains 8 warm requests with reused tokens whose reported 'prefill' rates span 39.6-555.7 tok/s; those are not cold prefills and are excluded from every comparison here

the sweep is one request per configuration point, except the 12719-token prompt which appears in five no-MTP sessions and one MTP session; those five no-MTP runs span four different argument vectors (--spec 4 with --adapt-async 1 or 0 and --pcie-frac absent or 0.20, and --spec 6 with --adapt-async 1 and --pcie-frac 0.20), so the 529.9-537.5 tok/s band is not a same-configuration repetition band. Only 19:13 and 19:20 share an identical vector (537.5, 537.4); a third launch with that vector measured 527.6 on a 12733-token prompt 1 h 41 min later. Three single-variable pairs exist in this family: --adapt-async 1 vs 0 (18:49:35 vs 18:57:26, 533.7 vs 529.9), --pcie-frac absent vs 0.20 (18:49:35 vs 19:04:16, 533.7 vs 531.9) and --spec 4 vs 6 (19:04:16 vs 19:13:24, 531.9 vs 537.5)

the MTP session (20:31:11) does not differ from every no-MTP session that ran the same 12719-token cold prompt by the same number of arguments: its argument vector differs by two flags from 19:13:24 and 19:20:29 (--mtp mtp/rt plus --vram-reserve-mib 768 vs 512), by three from 19:04:16 (also --spec 6 vs 4), by four from 18:49:35 (also --pcie-frac absent vs 0.20) and by five from 18:57:26 (also --adapt-async 1 vs 0). The MTP effect is not isolated against any of them, and the confounding grows the further the comparison moves from 19:13/19:20
no peak RAM or VRAM measurement was captured for these sessions; only the engine's own self-reported allocations are available
the machine was concurrently running interactive agent workloads during the sweep; the engine was the only inference process but not the only load
